arxiv-2104-11314.title: Ordered intricacy of Shilnikov saddle-focus homoclinics in symmetric systems
arxiv-2104-11314.creator: Tingli Xing, Krishna Pusuluri, Andrey L. Shilnikov
arxiv-2104-11314.description: Abstract Using the technique of Poincaré return maps, we disclose an intricate order of the subsequent homoclinics near the primary homoclinic bifurcation of the Shilnikov saddle-focus in systems with reflection symmetry. We also reveal the admissible shapes of the corresponding bifurcation curves in a parameter plane of such systems.

arxiv-2208-10585.title: Observation of dense collisional soliton complexes in a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate
arxiv-2208-10585.creator: Sean M. Mossman, Garyfallia C. Katsimiga, Simeon I. Mistakidis, Alejandro Romero-Ros, Thomas M. Bersano, Peter Schmelcher, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Peter Engels
arxiv-2208-10585.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sean M. Mossman, Garyfallia C. Katsimiga, Simeon I. Mistakidis, Alejandro Romero-Ros, Thomas M. Bersano, Peter Schmelcher, Panayotis G. Kevrekidis, Peter Engels. Abstract Solitons are nonlinear solitary waves which maintain their shape over time and through collisions, occurring in a variety of nonlinear media from plasmas to optics. We present an experimental and theoretical study of hydrodynamic phenomena in a two-component atomic Bose-Einstein condensate where a soliton array emerges from the imprinting of a periodic spin pattern by a microwave pulse-based winding technique.

arxiv-2211-14727.title: The q q -Racah polynomials from scalar products of Bethe states
arxiv-2211-14727.creator: Pascal Baseilhac ∗, Rodrigo A. Pimenta ∗∗
arxiv-2211-14727.description: Abstract . The q q -Racah polynomials are expressed in terms of certain ratios of scalar products of Bethe states associated with Bethe equations of either homogeneous or inhomogeneous type. This result is obtained by combining the theory of Leonard pairs and the modified algebraic Bethe ansatz. MSC: 33D45; 81R50; 81U15.

arxiv-2301-04085.title: Propagating photo- z z uncertainties: a functional derivative approach Propagating photo- z z uncertainties: a functional derivative approach – F 2022
arxiv-2301-04085.creator: Robert Reischke
arxiv-2301-04085.description: Abstract Photometric redshifts are a key ingredient in the analysis and interpretation of large-scale structure (LSS) surveys. The accuracy and precision of these redshift estimates are directly linked to the constraining power of photometric surveys. It is hence necessary to define precision and accuracy requirements for the redshift calibration to not infer biased results in the final analysis.

arxiv-2311-03322.title: Infinite Primes From Integer Partitions
arxiv-2311-03322.creator: Anton Shakov
arxiv-2311-03322.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Anton Shakov. Ferrers diagrams [ 1 ] are used to visually represent integer partitions. We describe a way to use Ferrers diagrams to uniquely represent integers in terms of their prime factors. This leads to a lower bound on the number of primes less than a given integer, namely π ⁡ ( x ) ≥ ⌊ lg ⁡ x ⌋ lg ⁡ ( ⌊ lg ⁡ x ⌋ + 1 ) \pi(x)\geq\frac{\lfloor\lg x\rfloor}{\lg(\lfloor\lg x\rfloor+1)} where π ⁡ ( x ) \pi(x) is the prime

arxiv-2312-09864.title: Accelerating Spatio-Textual Queries with Learned Indices
arxiv-2312-09864.creator: Georgios Chatzigeorgakidis, Kostas Patroumpas, Dimitrios Skoutas, Spiros Athanasiou
arxiv-2312-09864.description: Abstract Efficiently computing spatio-textual queries has become increasingly important in various applications that need to quickly retrieve geolocated entities associated with textual information, such as in location-based services and social networks. To accelerate such queries, several works have proposed combining spatial and textual indices into hybrid index structures.

arxiv-2404-02184.title: What is to Be Gained by Ensemble Models in Analysis of Spectroscopic Data?
arxiv-2404-02184.creator: Katarina Domijan
arxiv-2404-02184.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Katarina Domijan. An empirical study was carried out to compare different implementations of ensemble models aimed at improving prediction in spectroscopic data. A wide range of candidate models were fitted to benchmark datasets from regression and classification settings. A statistical analysis using linear mixed model was carried out on prediction performance criteria resulting from model fits over random splits of the data. The results showed that the ensemble classifiers were able to consistently outperform candidate models in our application.

arxiv-2410-04431.title: A Structural Approach to Growth-at-Risk Thanks: Acknowledgments: I am indebted to Christian Brownlees and Andrea Caggese for their support and guidance. I would also like to thank Geert Mesters, Barbara Rossi, Vladislav Morozov, Valeria Gargiulo and the participants of the 48th Symposium of the Span
arxiv-2410-04431.creator: Robert Wojciechowski
arxiv-2410-04431.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Robert Wojciechowski. We identify the structural impulse responses of quantiles of the outcome variable to a shock. Our estimation strategy explicitly distinguishes treatment from control variables, allowing us to model responses of unconditional quantiles while using controls for identification. Disentangling the effect of adding control variables on identification versus interpretation brings our structural quantile impulse responses conceptually closer to structural mean impulse responses.

arxiv-2410-09425.title: Computational complexity of the recoverable robust shortest path problem in acyclic digraphs under interval budgeted uncertainty
arxiv-2410-09425.creator: Marcel Jackiewicz, Adam Kasperski, Paweł Zieliński
arxiv-2410-09425.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the recoverable robust shortest path problem in acyclic digraphs, employing interval budgeted uncertainty to model uncertain second-stage costs. For the continuous budgeted uncertainty model, we prove that the problem is strongly NP-hard even in layered digraphs.

arxiv-2510-17492.title: A theory for self-sustained balanced states
arxiv-2510-17492.creator: in absence of strong external currents
arxiv-2510-17492.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by in absence of strong external currents. Abstract Recurrent neural networks with balanced excitation and inhibition exhibit irregular asynchronous dynamics, which is fundamental for cortical computations. Classical balance mechanisms require strong external inputs to sustain finite firing rates, raising concerns about their biological plausibility. Here, we investigate an alternative mechanism based on short-term synaptic depression (STD) acting on excitatory-excitatory synapses, which dynamically balances the network activity without the need of external inputs.

arxiv-2510-26834.title: Diffusion-Driven Generation of Minimally Preprocessed Brain MRI
arxiv-2510-26834.creator: Samuel W. Remedios, Aaron Carass, Jerry L. Prince, Blake E. Dewey, for the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative ∗, for the Australian Imaging Biomarkers and Lifestyle Flagship Study of Aging †, for the Health and Aging Brain Study (HABS-HD) Study Team ‡, for the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging §
arxiv-2510-26834.description: Abstract Purpose: To present and compare three denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) that generate 3D T 1 T_{1} -weighted MRI human brain images. Materials and methods: In this study, three DDPMs were trained using 80,675 80,675 image volumes from 42,406 42,406 subjects spanning 38 38 publicly available brain MRI datasets.

arxiv-2512-04771.title: Complementary Characterization of Agent-Based Models via Computational Mechanics and Diffusion Models
arxiv-2512-04771.creator: Roberto Garrone
arxiv-2512-04771.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Roberto Garrone. This article extends the preprint Characterizing Agent-Based Model Dynamics via ϵ \epsilon -Machines and Kolmogorov-Style Complexity by introducing diffusion models as orthogonal and complementary tools for characterizing the output of agent-based models (ABMs). Where ϵ \epsilon -machines capture the predictive temporal structure and intrinsic computation of ABM-generated time series, diffusion models characterize high-dimensional cross-sectional distributions, learn underlying data manifolds, and enable synthetic generation of plausible population-level outcomes.

arxiv-2601-13048.title: Analysis of Long Range Dependency Understanding in State Space Models
arxiv-2601-13048.creator: Srividya Ravikumar, Abhinav Anand, Shweta Verma, Mira Mezini
arxiv-2601-13048.description: Abstract Although state-space models (SSMs) have demonstrated strong performance on long-sequence benchmarks, most research has emphasized predictive accuracy rather than interpretability. In this work, we present the first systematic kernel interpretability study of the diagonalized state-space model (S4D) trained on a real-world task (vulnerability detection in source code).

pmc-10671283.title: Biodegradation of Poly(ethylene terephthalate) by Bacillus safensis YX8
pmc-10671283.creator: Caiting Zeng, Fanghui Ding, Jie Zhou, Weiliang Dong, Zhongli Cui, Xin Yan
pmc-10671283.description: Due to the extensive utilization of poly (ethylene terephthalate) (PET), a significant amount of PET waste has been discharged into the environment, endangering both human health and the ecology. As an eco-friendly approach to PET waste treatment, biodegradation is dependent on efficient strains and enzymes.

pmc-11341044.title: Digital transformation in college libraries: The effect of digital reading on reader service satisfaction
pmc-11341044.creator: Yixin Lu, Shengguang Lin
pmc-11341044.description: In the pursuit of digital transformation, college libraries have increasingly embraced the promotion of digital reading as a critical initiative. While numerous studies have delved into the strategies employed by college libraries in their digital transformation endeavors, there remains a lack of research elucidating the direct influence of digital reading on reader service satisfaction within these institutions.

pmc-11493190.title: Ultrasound-assisted extraction of scopolamine and hyoscyamine from Hyoscyamus niger roots using central compost design
pmc-11493190.creator: Roghayeh Ahmadpour, Bahram Maleki Zanjani, Ghasem-ali Garoosi, Reza Farjaminezhad, Raheem Haddad
pmc-11493190.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Hyoscyamus niger is an important medicinal plant used in medicine and contains tropane alkaloid compounds such as hyoscyamine and scopolamine. In this study, after the selection of the solvent for extracting hyoscyamine and scopolamine, the central composite design of the response surface methodology was used to study the effect of solvent concentrations (0, 25, 50, 75, and 100 %), temperatures (25, 30, 35, 40, and 45 °C) and ultrasonication times (10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 min).

pmc-11613273.title: High-Affinity Peptides for Target Protein Screened in Ultralarge Virtual Libraries
pmc-11613273.creator: Boyuan Xue, Ruixue Li, Zhao Cheng, Xiaohong Zhou
pmc-11613273.description: High-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) has emerged as a pivotal strategy for identifying high-affinity peptides targeting functional proteins, which are crucial for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. In the HTVS of peptides, expanding the library capacity to enhance peptide sequence diversity, thereby screening out excellent affinity peptide candidates, remains a significant challenge.

pmc-11660187.title: Efficacy and Safety of Optilume Drug-Coated Balloon for Urethral Stricture Treatment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11660187.creator: Peter Estaphanous, Ahmed O Khalifa, Youstina Makar
pmc-11660187.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The Optilume drug-coated balloon (DCB) (North Plymouth, USA) is a novel treatment option for urethral stricture disease that combines mechanical dilation with localized delivery of paclitaxel, an antiproliferative drug aimed at reducing recurrence rates by inhibiting scar tissue formation. This systematic review and meta-analysis, conducted using studies published in the last 10 years up to November 2024, assessed the efficacy and safety of Optilume DCB across seven studies involving 457 patients.

pmc-12461916.title: Size Dependent Uncatalyzed Sulfite Oxidation in Aqueous Microdroplets
pmc-12461916.creator: Kedong Gong, Sandhya Sethuraman, Adriane Tam, Zifeng Tang, V. Faye McNeill, Vicki H. Grassian
pmc-12461916.description: Aqueous aerosols and microdroplets exhibit unique chemical kinetics relative to the bulk phase, impacting air quality and climate via multiphase atmospheric processes. Here, we investigate uncatalyzed oxidation of sulfite to sulfate by O2 in aqueous microdroplets deposited on a superhydrophobic substrate, as a function of size, gas-phase composition, and temperature utilizing in situ micro-Raman spectroscopy.

pmc-12547708.title: Enabling informed decisions for climate risk and crisis management. The BRACE review protocol
pmc-12547708.creator: Melania Michetti, Alexandra D’Angelo
pmc-12547708.description: This article outlines a structured and replicable systematic review process (BRACE) aimed at mapping global research trends on barriers and enablers to climate change adaptation. The focus is on climate hazards—floods, droughts, and heatwaves—within the frameworks of Risk Reduction (RR) and Crisis Management (CM), with attention to governance and socioeconomic factors.

pmc-12790229.title: Cardiac Injury Causing Traumatic Ventricular Septal Rupture With Right Ventricular Pseudoaneurysm
pmc-12790229.creator: Mahima Tyagi, Matthew Shotwell, Amelia E Power, Gurnoor Singh, Dinesh K Kalra
pmc-12790229.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundVentricular septal rupture (VSR) is a rare, potentially fatal consequence of blunt cardiac injury (BCI). Concomitant right ventricular (RV) pseudoaneurysm formation is even rarer, and the occurrence of both complications has not to our knowledge been previously reported.Case SummaryA 63-year-old man presented with a VSR and a torn tricuspid chord, flail leaflet, and severe tricuspid regurgitation after BCI due to a motor vehicle accident. He declined surgery initially and presented a month later with severe heart failure symptoms.

pmc-13272289.title: Health effects of black and blond tobacco: a comparative analysis on smoking-related diseases with emphasis on bronchitis and COPD
pmc-13272289.creator: María Bejarano-Vila, Irene Abad-Perez, Daniel Bautista, Francisco Bosch-Morell, Isabel Martinez-Solis
pmc-13272289.description: BackgroundThere is ample scientific evidence to support that tobacco consumption is associated with diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), bronchitis, and cancer. However, few studies have compared the harm caused by different types of tobacco, such as black and blond tobacco (BlaT, BloT).

pmc-13395555.title: Material-dependent oxygen transport governs ischemia-reperfusion injury and drug response in a kidney microphysiological system
pmc-13395555.creator: Naokata Kutsuzawa, Hiroko Nakamura, Kenta Shinha, Hiroshi Kimura
pmc-13395555.description: Oxygen availability is a critical yet often overlooked factor in cell culture, and discrepancies between nominal oxygen settings and the actual cellular microenvironment can compromise model validity. This limitation is particularly relevant in modeling ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury, where dynamic changes in oxygen supply critically influence cellular responses.

pmc-13551939.title: Multi-scale hierarchical regulation of starch chain length distribution and its consequential impact on starch digestibility: From molecular structure to granular degradation
pmc-13551939.creator: Zixuan Liu, Tianshuang Xia, Chunfan Guo, Jingxuan Ma, Mingyue Chen, Zhaoxia Wu
pmc-13551939.description: Starch chain length distribution (CLD) hierarchically modulates starch digestibility from enzyme recognition to granular degradation. This review summarizes CLD characteristics of amylose (short, medium, long chains) and amylopectin (A, B1, B2, B3 chains). The hierarchical regulatory rules are elucidated at molecular (chain flexibility, hydrogen bonding), aggregated (double helix, crystalline-amorphous regions), and granular (morphology, pores) scales.
